auth.title: Sign in
auth.lead: Orgpuls is for employees and managers in your organisation.

app.name: Orgpuls
app.tagline: Psychosocial work environment for Norwegian organisations. Answers are stored in Norway, and no single answer can be traced back to a person.

ytring.label: Freedom to speak up
ytring.desc: Whether you dare to speak up — about mistakes, about disagreement, about what is not working — and whether anything happens when you do. It is not the same as everyone agreeing.
ytring.s1: I can report censurable conditions without fearing consequences
ytring.s2: When someone reports a problem, something is done about it
ytring.s3: Disagreement is raised openly here, not in the corridor afterwards

mengde.label: Workload and time pressure
mengde.desc: The relationship between what has to be done and the time, people and equipment you actually have. Sustained imbalance is the most common cause of health-damaging strain.
mengde.s1: My workload is manageable over time
mengde.s2: I have enough time to do the job well enough
mengde.s3: I can switch off from work when the working day is over

motstrid.label: Conflicting demands
motstrid.desc: When two managers, two systems or two concerns ask for things that do not go together, and no one says what should give way.
motstrid.s1: I rarely get tasks without knowing what should be deprioritised
motstrid.s2: The demands from different quarters hang together
motstrid.s3: I know who decides when two things collide

kontakt.label: Contact and communication
kontakt.desc: Whether the work allows contact with others. Working alone brings both social isolation and a safety risk — you must be able to call for help.
kontakt.s1: I have the opportunity for contact with colleagues during the working day
kontakt.s2: I can call for help quickly if something happens while I am alone
kontakt.s3: I do not feel isolated in my job

emosjon.label: Emotional demands
emosjon.desc: The strain of facing demanding encounters with people — customers, users, colleagues — or of having to conceal your own reactions.
emosjon.s1: I am rarely left alone in emotionally demanding situations
emosjon.s2: We talk about difficult incidents afterwards
emosjon.s3: I am allowed to react as a human being at work

leder.label: Support from manager
leder.desc: Whether the manager is available when things get difficult, and whether the support is practical rather than merely well-meaning.
leder.s1: I get support from my manager when the job becomes demanding
leder.s2: My manager knows enough about what my job actually involves
leder.s3: I can raise difficult matters with my manager

medvirk.label: Participation and control
medvirk.desc: Influence over your own working day: order, pace, method — and over changes that affect you.
medvirk.s1: I have influence over how I carry out my work
medvirk.s2: I am heard when something is to be changed
medvirk.s3: I can influence the pace of my own work

integritet.label: Integrity and dignity
integritet.desc: Whether people are met with respect and equality, whether their boundaries are upheld, and whether they may exercise their own professional and ethical judgement. This is also the legal basis for protection against harassment.
integritet.s1: I am met with respect regardless of who I am
integritet.s2: I may use professional judgement when I think something should be done differently
integritet.s3: My boundaries for privacy are respected at work

rolle.label: Role clarity
rolle.desc: Whether you know what is expected, where your responsibility ends, and what counts as good enough.
rolle.s1: I know what is expected of me in my job
rolle.s2: I know where my responsibility ends and others begin
rolle.s3: I know what counts as good work here

kollega.label: Support from colleagues
kollega.desc: Whether people actually turn up for one another in practice, not just in speeches.
kollega.s1: My colleagues turn up when I need help
kollega.s2: We share knowledge instead of holding on to it
kollega.s3: I feel like part of the team

mening.label: Recognition and meaning
mening.desc: Whether the work feels meaningful and whether effort is seen by someone who matters.
mening.s3: I am proud to work here

malinger.title: Measurements
malinger.lead: One baseline a year covers the duty to survey. The pulses in between measure only what you have put actions on — five questions, under a minute.
malinger.cardRoundSub: Closed {date} · no further answers are coming in
malinger.thinNote: below threshold — shown only as participation, never as a result
malinger.privacy: The system knows who has not answered, so that the reminder goes only there. No one in the organisation can see that list — not you, not the managers, not the safety representative. The link between person and answer does not exist in the database.
malinger.reminderClosed: Reminders can only be sent while a round is open.
malinger.qsLead: Eleven factors — the same ones the Working Environment Act § 4-3 and the regulation name after the clarification of 1 January 2026, phrased in QPS Nordic language. Three statements per factor, answered 1–5. You may switch a factor off, but not change the wording — it is the wording that makes the figures comparable over time and against the industry.

anbefaling.label: Recommendation question
anbefaling.text: How likely is it that you would recommend us as a place to work to someone you know?
anbefaling.note: Answered 1–5. Reported as a figure of its own, not as part of the index.

krenkende.label: Offensive behaviour
krenkende.text: Have you experienced or seen offensive behaviour, harassment or bullying at work in the last twelve months?
krenkende.note: Yes / no / prefer not to answer. Shown only as a count for the whole organisation, never per group.
krenkende.o3: Yes, saw others subjected to it

vold.label: Violence and threats
vold.text: Have you experienced violence or threats at work in the last twelve months?
vold.note: The same rule: counts only, never broken down.

apent_felt.label: Open field
apent_felt.text: What should we do something about first?
apent_felt.note: Voluntary. Grouped by theme and checked for identifying detail before anyone reads it.

respond.commentPrompt: Want to say more? Voluntary and anonymous
respond.openNote: Voluntary. The text is grouped by theme and checked for identifying detail before anyone reads it.
respond.doneTitle: Thank you. That took four minutes.
respond.doneLead: Your answer is anonymous. Your manager sees only figures once at least {threshold} have answered.
respond.promise1: Your answer is anonymous. Name, email and IP are not stored with what you answer.
respond.promise2: Your manager sees figures only once at least {threshold} in the group have answered.
respond.promise3: You can skip questions, and you can answer on your phone during a break.
respond.promise4: If you write a comment, your manager can reply without learning who you are.
respond.invalidLead: The link has been used, has expired, or is wrong. If you have already answered, your answer is recorded — you cannot answer again.
respond.submitFailed: Your answer was not sent. Please try again.

rapport.title: Report
rapport.lead: One basis, four recipients. Choose who the report is for — the content changes with it.

audienceNote.tilsyn: Full documentation with legal bases, method, participation and signature fields. This is the version you present at an inspection.
audienceNote.amu: A committee paper with a recommendation and room for the minutes. Without individual comments.
audienceNote.ledelse: Two pages: the figures, the three priorities, and what they cost in time. Without statutory references.
audienceNote.ansatte: Plain language, no figures below the threshold, no quotes that could be traced. Giving this back is what makes people answer next time.

docTitle.tilsyn: Documentation of systematic work on the psychosocial working environment
docTitle.amu: Paper for the working environment committee — psychosocial working environment {year}
docTitle.ansatte: This is what you said — and this is what we are doing

docLead.tilsyn: Prepared under the Working Environment Act § 3-1 (c) and § 4-3, and the regulation on the performance of work, part two chapter 1A. The document covers the survey and risk assessment of the psychosocial working environment — not the undertaking's other health and safety duties. It shows the survey, the risk assessment, the measures and the effect assessment for the period.
docLead.amu: A committee paper with findings, risk assessment and proposed measures. The safety representative and the union representatives have reviewed it before the meeting.
docLead.ledelse: A short account of where the undertaking stands, what weighs it down most, and what has been decided.
docLead.ansatte: Everyone who answered should know what came of it. This is the feedback to the whole undertaking.

rapport.omfangOrg: The whole organisation · {count, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}}
rapport.instrumentBody: Eleven psychosocial working environment factors, three statements per factor, answered on a five-point scale. The wording builds on QPS Nordic and covers the factors the regulation names. In addition one recommendation question, screening for offensive behaviour and for violence and threats, and one open field.
rapport.gjennomforingBody: {kind} sent {sent}, closed {closed}. {answered} of {total} employees answered, {pct} per cent. The answers are anonymous and stored with no link to a person.
rapport.terskelBody: Results are not shown for groups with fewer than {threshold} answers.
rapport.terskelWithheld: {groups} is therefore included only in the whole, not as a group of its own.
rapport.section2Lead: The measurements included in this report, and those left out.
rapport.runScope: {questions, plural, other {# questions}} · {factors, plural, other {# factors}}
rapport.idxLine: Overall working environment index {index} of 100, against {prev} in {prevYear}. The answers are converted from a five-point scale to an index from 0 to 100.
rapport.idxLineFirst: Overall working environment index {index} of 100, the first complete baseline. The answers are converted from a five-point scale to an index from 0 to 100.
rapport.idxLineTeam: Groups with fewer than {threshold} answers are not broken out.
rapport.ansatteAnonymity: No figure in this report can be traced back to an individual. Groups with fewer than five answers are not shown on their own. If you wrote a comment, your manager's reply is in the app.
rapport.noData: No measurement in {year} has enough answers to be reported.
rapport.section4Lead: Likelihood of an undesirable condition assessed against its consequence for health, safety and welfare.
rapport.section4Empty: The survey has not been risk-assessed. § 3-1 letter c requires that conditions be assessed on the basis of the survey; this report documents the survey, not the assessment.
rapport.section5Empty: No measure is linked to the measurements in this period.

tiltak.title: Measures
tiltak.lead: Every measure hangs on a factor and cannot be closed before its effect has been measured. That is the documentation the Labour Inspection Authority asks for.
tiltak.emptyLead: Change the status or the measurement to see the others.

kindNote.kollektivt: Aimed at how the work is organised. This is what the law prefers.
kindNote.individuelt: The Labour Inspection Authority asks that collective measures be considered first. An individual measure should be justified.

problem.noOrg: No organisation was found to attach the measure to.

lead.grunnlinje: The whole question set, once a year. This is the measurement Arbeidstilsynet asks for, and the one that sets the zero point everything else is measured against.
lead.puls: A few questions between baselines, about what you have taken measures on. Measures whether the measures work.
lead.oppfolging: One factor in depth, when you need to know more about something specific.

grunnlinje.note: {count, plural, other {# questions}} · annual · meets the statutory duty

oppfolging.label: Follow-up
oppfolging.note: one factor in depth · as needed

maleoppsett.factorNote: The baseline uses all eleven. The wording is fixed — it is what makes the figures comparable with last year and with the industry.
maleoppsett.commentLead: The figures say where it hurts. The comments say why. You decide here where they can be written.

hvert.label: On every question
hvert.note: A comment field under every statement. Gathers the most text, and the most noise.

lave.label: Only on low answers
lave.note: The field appears when somebody answers 1 or 2. Lands where it hurts.

slutt.label: One open field at the end
slutt.note: Calmest for the respondent. You lose the link to which factor it concerns.

av.label: Off
av.note: No free text. Then you have only figures to go on.

maleoppsett.dialogue: Allow anonymous two-way conversation on comments
maleoppsett.dialogueOn: A leader can reply to a comment without learning who wrote it, and the employee can reply back. The conversation lives in Samtaler.
maleoppsett.dialogueOff: Comments are read but not answered. Whoever wrote one never learns whether anybody saw it.
maleoppsett.groupHeadAnswered: {count, plural, one {# employee} other {# employees}} · {answered} responded last time
maleoppsett.groupWarnThin: {group} got {answered} responses last time — below the threshold of {threshold}. The group receives the questions but appears only as part of the whole, not as its own row.
maleoppsett.groupWarnNone: Groups with fewer than {threshold} responses appear only as part of the whole, never as their own row.
maleoppsett.ownNote: Your own questions let you ask about something happening right now: a reorganisation, a new tool, a measure you want to know landed.
maleoppsett.ownFull: Five is the cap. Every question beyond it costs response rate, and the fixed factors are what give you the comparison.
maleoppsett.suggest1: Do you know what was decided after the last measurement?
maleoppsett.suggest2: Have you seen changes at work since the last measurement?
maleoppsett.suggest3: Does the new planning tool work for you?
maleoppsett.consentLead: A recurring measurement with per-group results counts as a control measure. Aml. § 9-2 then makes three demands: discussion beforehand, information to those affected, and regular evaluation of whether the arrangement is still needed.
maleoppsett.vo: The verneombud is consulted on the setup
maleoppsett.voNote: The verneombud is consulted on the setup, not merely told about it, and sees the result at the same time as management. Aml. § 6-2 fourth paragraph.
maleoppsett.tv: Need and design discussed with the elected representatives
maleoppsett.infoHead: What employees are told before it goes out
maleoppsett.infoLaw: aml. § 9-2 second paragraph — purpose, practical consequences and expected duration
maleoppsett.infoPurposeValue: To survey the psychosocial work environment and document a risk assessment under aml. § 3-1 letter c.
maleoppsett.infoConsequenceValue: Answers are anonymous. Results appear per group only at {threshold} responses, never per person.
maleoppsett.infoDurationValue: Annual, ongoing until the arrangement is changed or ended.
maleoppsett.evalLaw: aml. § 9-2 third paragraph — the need must be assessed regularly, together with the elected representatives

summaryEval.hver_6_mnd: Evaluated every 6 months with the elected representatives
summaryEval.arlig: Evaluated annually with the elected representatives
summaryEval.etter_hver_runde: Evaluated after every round with the elected representatives

maleoppsett.summaryLegal: Meets the survey duty in aml. § 3-1 c and § 4-3, cf. the regulation chapter 1A

samtaler.lead: {count, plural, one {# comment is waiting} other {# comments are waiting}} for a reply. The oldest has waited {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
samtaler.leadClear: No comments are waiting for a reply right now.
samtaler.emptyLead: Change the filter to see the others.
samtaler.waiting: Waiting {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}
samtaler.varselNote: This may be a notification under aml. chapter 2A. Do reply here, but the case must be handled through the whistleblowing procedure — not as an ordinary work-environment measure.
samtaler.replyPlaceholder: Reply anonymously — whoever wrote it gets this in the app …
samtaler.rule1: You never see who wrote it. Your reply reaches the app of whoever wrote it, without the identity being revealed either way.
samtaler.rule2: Comments below the threshold of {threshold} are not shown at all — they are individual statements, not group statistics.
samtaler.rule3: The verneombud does not see comments unless you share them.
samtaler.rule4: Comments that may be notifications under aml. chapter 2A are marked, and must be handled through the whistleblowing procedure — not here.
